Well, for the most part, I'd guess they probably think "Gee, Richard
Garfield really _is_ that good", plus a good dose of "White Wolf knows what
they're doing..."

I can get on board with some people's feelings that VTES hasn't grown to
the scale of a VS. or MTG because of its more grassroots structure, but
that same organization is what is apparently allowing it to last in the
long-term...

One other thought. We might need to think about migrating the primary VTES
community off of Usenet. There's too few people out there who remember
what Usenet is, nevermind how to access it... Google Groups cruddy
interface doesn't help much, nor does our out-dated group name. Don't get
me wrong, I love Usenet dearly, but being here, as opposed to a web-based
forum hurts our visibility and accessibility for new players...

If something like that were to be done, it'd have to be a conscious
action, organized and planned by the whole community.

DaveZ

I get it, and thats why I said what I did. Follow along with me, if you
will. My issue isn't with Usenet. Its with VTES's reduced visibility
because Usenet is where most experienced players are posting. This
community, as great as it is, as great as Usenet is, is buried _deep_
relative to the competition. We all may like it that way (I note the
astounding signal to noise ratio of the group), but to the rest of the CCG
community (potential VTES players) it would seem like this game's player
base is non-existant. I think this issue plays in to the whole "VTES?
Wasn't that game disontinued?" schtick that plays out every 6-12 months...
We've actually got quite a few players in VTES now (guessing maybe 15 to
25K worldwide total players), but nobody would know it, given their low
profile online.

>
>> nor does our out-dated group name. Don't get
>> me wrong, I love Usenet dearly, but being here, as opposed to a
>> web-based forum hurts our visibility and accessibility for new
>> players...
>

> How did you plan to search for LSJ's rulings in a web based forum, as
> opposed to a Google-archived Usenet group?
>

How about WW step up, and archive LSJ posts on an independent web-based
rules search engine? ...and seperate the wheat from the chaff of outdated
rulings while they're at it.
Regardless of the answer to your counter-question, you haven't addressed
my primary concern, which is that the visibility of VTES is suffereing for
having its best and brightest posting here, instead of at, say a VTES sub-
forum at tcgplayer.com, for greater visibility wrt other games... tcgplayer
gets 14 million page views and about 725,000 unique visitors (potential
VTES players) each month. We're not growing as fast as we should(could) as
a community of players, because a large number of potential players don't
know where to find us.
I think it'd be a fantastic idea for VTES to advertise there in a banner
ad campaign for 3rd Edition, the Player's Kit, and the upcoming Sword of
Caine, use the clout of being an advertiser to negotiate for a sub-forum to
be created for VTES (usually, a new game has to show some level of activity
in an "other games" super-buried sub-sub forum, before getting their own
board), and then get us, the VTES players, to populate the hell out of that
board as an additional means of attracting new players from other games.
Its a classic marketing tactic. If you're Burger King, the best place to
be is right next to McDonalds. If you're Target, you want to be next to a
Wal-Mart, etc. Since the VTES community is not as a whole, being greatly
supported by brick and mortar game stores, and its presence is largely
online, that presence is our single largest asset in promoting VTES, and
we're sqandering it by keeping to our own little out-of-the-way corner of
the Internet circa 1994. Hope the analogy is understood, I cannot tell
from your headers if my US-based examples are appropriate.

Regards,
DaveZ
Atom Weaver

Eww. I just went there. Poked around. That site is hideous. Everything

I'm unclear on what kind of advantage could be gained by having
discussion there. Like, the two options are likely:

A) Attempt to move *all* VTES discussion to a place like this, which is
unlikely to happen, as folks aren't going to stop posting on the WW
forum or usenet.

B) Just have a token presence there that is going to further dilute
discussion, as people discuss across usenet, the WW forum, the VTES
list-serve, and then wherever the the new forum is.

Given that it is unlikely that WW will fold their forum in the name of
moving traffic to a non WW forum, and it is unlikely that all the old
cranky guys will give up usenet, the end result is probably option B. Is
having a token presence on some abomnible site like TCGplayer.com really
worth the effort? I realize that it'll probably increase visibility
some, but more so, than, like, articles in Scrye and just general
advertising?

Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:
> Given that it is unlikely that WW will fold their forum in the name of

> having a token presence on some abomnible site like TCGplayer.com really
> worth the effort? I realize that it'll probably increase visibility
> some, but more so, than, like, articles in Scrye and just general
> advertising?

Due to bizarrely skewed market for VTES that is highly internet
dependant, I think that it would generate much more
traffic/visibility/awareness than an article in Scryre.

My thoughts on this are
1) You can't buy VTES cards from Scrye, you can buy them on the
internet.
2) You can't have a discussion with Scrye about the game, but you can
on the internet.

In the advertising world, the traditional means of advertising are
shrinking currently (print, radio, and television) as internet usage
goes up. No one has figured out how to advertise because
advertisements are monodirectional (i.e. it gives you a message, but
doesn't respond to your reactions to that message). The internet is a
dialogue and as such no one has really figured out the best way to
advertise on it. Moving a active "intellectual" community to a high
traffic area, potentially, has the prospect of being the ideal form of
internet advertising that gets traffic/visibility/awareness.

Just my 2 cents.

towards raising the game's image and visibility, and increase the
liklihood that someone might decide to try it out.

> Like, the two options are likely:
>
> A) Attempt to move *all* VTES discussion to a place like this, which
> is unlikely to happen, as folks aren't going to stop posting on the WW
> forum or usenet.
>
> B) Just have a token presence there that is going to further dilute
> discussion, as people discuss across usenet, the WW forum, the VTES
> list-serve, and then wherever the the new forum is.
>
> Given that it is unlikely that WW will fold their forum in the name of
> moving traffic to a non WW forum, and it is unlikely that all the old
> cranky guys will give up usenet, the end result is probably option B.
> Is having a token presence on some abomnible site like TCGplayer.com
> really worth the effort?

Right, a token effort will just die out after a while, make the game
look lame, and further perpetuate the mis-conceptions about the health
of the game... which is why I started this whole side thread with all
that talk about migration having to be a conscious and organized effort
by the players etc. And I'm only talking about the Usenet group
migrating somewhere more visible. Moving the WW forum would be
untenable, as the game's maker would wnat to continue to have its
presence on their website (show of support for the line, yadda yadda),
although they might do something like the place-holder link they have
for EVE, but even then, I don't think that's a good idea.

> I realize that it'll probably increase visibility
> some, but more so, than, like, articles in Scrye and just general
> advertising?
>

Ads and articles aren't a community, they give you no sense of whether
the game is played or not, and very little idea of how... Games are all
about opponents and competition, and people interacting, and a lot of
the appeal of VTES is in the community that has grown up around the
game.

DaveZ
Atom Weaver

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
atomweaver <atomw...@hotmail.com> writes:

> One other thought. We might need to think about migrating the
> primary VTES community off of Usenet.

(I missed Dave's actual message, so I am replying through Jaane's

message. Damn my newsreader for deleting read messages! No, wait. I like
that it does that...)

In any case, I don't think this is actually necessary. Yeah, having to
go through google.groups if you can't manage or figure out a newsreader
is kind of sub optimal (heck, I know all about usenet and newsreaders,
and it took me, like, 2 years to get my newsreader back up and running
after switching from dial up to high speed, as it is incredibly

difficult to find information on news servers from Roadrunner). But that
being said, I'm wildly unconvinced that google.groups is significantly
less optimal than web based forums.

Comparing the google.groups interface to the newsgroup to, say, the
White Wolf VTES forum, I *vastly* prefer google.groups as a forum for
discussion. Maybe I'm just a cranky old guy, but I find all the bells
and whistles (sexy graphics, avatars, whatever) to be both unnecessary
and kind of annoying. Heck--I'm using high speed internet, and loading
and posting to the WW Forum is *still* irritatingly slow. I find the
goofy little animated avatars to be just annoying. I find the graphic
smiley faces to be really annoying. I find the whole experience of the
sexy graphic high end design to be just unnecessary. Not that the WW
VTES forum is badly designed--it is actually quite nicely designed, in a
visual sense, and perfectly functional, but it is, for my money, klunky
and the sexiness actually hinders the functionality. But even then, it
is still there and gets a pretty reasonable amount of traffic.

If we assume that most non-cranky old guys are going to access the
newsgroup through google.groups (as it is easier to access than a
newsreader), other than lacking the sexy graphics, google.groups works
just fine as an interface. Yeah, it goes down once and a while, but so
does the web forum.

In the end here, my point is simply that as an interface, google.groups
isn't super optimal, but it is accessible enough and simple enough that
if people just know to go there to look for information on VTES, it is
just as viable, if not more so, than a web forum.

Yeah, the name is a slight stumbling block, but it isn't that difficult
to get folks pointed in the right direction--the WW site has a link, the
Lasombra's site has a lot of pointer information, the rulebooks have
pointer information, and occasionally, folks like me will post pointer
information in the web forum.


